target.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running browser screenshot with a configured image-understanding model would have the session become unusable when that vision model failed: later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` tool results were framed as image analysis until `/new`.

The vision-failure path previously fell back to injecting a raw base64 image block into the tool result. That image-bearing result is retained across recent completed turns, so it keeps re-entering model context and contaminates subsequent tool use.

This is the failure path described in #106703 (and the same root cause reported in #105305).

## Why This Change Was Made

The vision success path already returns a text-only description. This change makes the configured-vision failure path consistent with it: on describe failure, return a text-only result that reports the failure reason and keeps the staged outbound-copy path so the screenshot can still be shared explicitly via the message tool. Never write base64 image data into session/tool-result state on that path.

Scoped intentionally:

- Configured vision model throws → text-only (fixed path). A user who configured image understanding opted into text descriptions, so a transient provider error should not silently switch to dumping raw base64.
- Image understanding skipped / not configured (`describeBrowserScreenshot` returns `null`) → still returns the raw image, so vision-capable primary models that rely on seeing the screenshot are unaffected.

## User Impact

When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the session stays usable: tool results remain text-framed, and the screenshot can still be shared via the message tool. Users without image understanding configured keep the previous model-visible screenshot behavior.

## Evidence

### Behavior repro against the real session-state code

The reported symptom is a session-state effect: the vision-failure screenshot result persists across turns and forces later tool results into image-analysis framing. The retention logic that governs this is `pruneProcessedHistoryImages` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.ts`), which keeps image blocks from the last `PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` completed turns intact.

`scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-session.ts` drives that real production transform over a realistic multi-turn session and contrasts the pre-fix tool-result shape (base64 image block, as `imageResultFromFile` emitted) with the post-fix shape (text-only, as this PR's catch path emits and as the unit tests below assert). It shows the recent vision-failure image survives history pruning and persists next to later `read` / `browser snapshot` results, while the text-only result leaves zero image blocks so later results stay text-framed.

Reproduce:

```
node --import tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-session.ts
```

Redacted transcript (content-block types only; no base64 bytes or paths are printed):

```
Repro: configured browser screenshot-vision failure and later tool results (#106703, #105305)
Mechanism: pruneProcessedHistoryImages keeps image blocks from the last 3 completed turns.
The screenshot sits inside that window, so retention alone does not remove a base64 image.

=== PRE-FIX handler output (imageResultFromFile: base64 image block) ===
session turns: 17 messages
prune activated (older images scrubbed): yes
tool results the model sees after prune:
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text,image]
  toolResult(read) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
image blocks persisting in model context: 1

=== POST-FIX handler output (text-only failure result) ===
session turns: 17 messages
prune activated (older images scrubbed): yes
tool results the model sees after prune:
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(read) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
image blocks persisting in model context: 0

=== verdict ===
PRE-FIX: 1 image block(s) persist next to later read/snapshot results -> session contaminated until /new.
POST-FIX: 0 image block(s) -> later read/browser-snapshot results stay text-framed.

result: PASS
```

The old turn-1 screenshot image is pruned (retention working), yet in the pre-fix run the recent vision-failure image is preserved and rides alongside the later `read` and `browser snapshot` results (`[text,image]`), which is the contamination. In the post-fix run that slot is `[text]` and no image block reaches model context, so later results stay text-framed.

Honesty note on scope: this environment could not run a fully-live browser node plus a real failing vision provider end to end. The repro therefore exercises the real retention transform (`pruneProcessedHistoryImages`) with the two upstream seams represented at their real boundaries: the screenshot tool-result shapes are exactly what the handler emits before/after this change (pre-fix `imageResultFromFile` image block; post-fix text-only, asserted by the tests below), and the later `read` / `browser snapshot` results are ordinary text tool results. The handler-side output shape is independently locked by the tests below and is visible in the diff.

### Handler-side unit and regression tests

Updated and added focused tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` (these drive the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot path):

- `defangs vision failure fallback text and stays text-only`: vision-failure result is text-only (no `imageResultFromFile`, no image content block, no `details.media`) while preserving the neutralized failure text and share hint.
- `never injects a raw image block when configured vision fails (#106703, #105305)`: configured-vision failure returns zero image content blocks and marks `details.vision.failed`, so the result cannot persist an image across turns.
- No-vision (skipped/unconfigured) path still returns the raw image with sanitization.

Local gate (redacted paths):

```
vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts        98 passed
vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/vision.test.ts        6 passed
vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.test.ts   12 passed

lint (scripts), format:check, tsgo scripts, tsgo extensions (prod), tsgo extensions (test): green
```

Closes #106703
Related #105305

target.title: feat(ui): Labs settings page for experimental feature toggles
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Experimental features (Code Mode today, Swarm next) are enabled only by hand-editing `openclaw.json`. There is no discoverable, safe place in the Control UI to try them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Part of the Swarm program (#110325): a Settings → Labs page gives experimental features one obvious home with clear "may change or break" framing, so gated features can ship dark on `main` and be flipped on deliberately.

## User Impact

New Settings → Labs page (Agents & Tools group). First entry: Code Mode — toggle reads both accepted config shapes (`tools.codeMode: true` boolean shorthand and object form) and writes an RFC 7396 merge-patch with an explicit `false` on disable (never a key delete). Registry-driven so future entries (Swarm, #110325) are one-liners; a Swarm entry is stubbed but not rendered until its config key exists in the schema.

![Labs settings page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/labs-page-0717/labs-settings.png)

## Evidence

- Focused vitest: `ui/src/pages/labs/labs-page.test.ts` + navigation tests — 58 passed (see checks).
- Fresh autoreview (codex gpt-5.6-sol, branch mode): clean, 0 findings, "patch is correct (0.94)".
- Live render verified against `pnpm dev:ui:mock` (screenshot above; toggle interaction is config-snapshot-gated, covered by unit tests for merge-patch correctness).
- i18n: en keys authored; foreign-locale sync follows the normal post-merge workflow.

target.title: Add experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the canonical Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report incomplete installs, missing or modified agents, workspace drift, package drift/incomplete state, MCP ownership drift, unresolved cron ownership, and orphaned subordinate rows
- corroborate cron ownership against every page of one stable live Gateway inventory snapshot
- preserve source MCP placeholders while inspecting runtime config so resolved credentials cannot create false drift
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution absent unless `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`

## Contract

- doctor reuses `claws status` ownership states instead of independently interpreting managed resources
- absent and pre-Claws state produce no Claw findings and no Claw-created state directory, database, schema, migration, chmod, checkpoint, or journal-mode change
- existing state is observed through one read-only handle; WAL-backed state remains visible, while missing experimental ownership tables are treated as empty only in read-only mode
- unreadable, invalid, or forward-version state databases return one structured error finding rather than aborting doctor
- source MCP config is read through the canonical source-config API; `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders remain unexpanded
- live cron health requires matching scheduler job id, declaration key, owner, enabled state, and execution-relevant digest; Gateway failure or a changing inventory reports `unknown`, never healthy
- the Claw collector is advisory and does not mutate config, files, scheduler state, provenance, database bytes, metadata, schema, or journal mode; OpenClaw's existing config-observation behavior outside this collector is unchanged

## Verification

- current-head GitHub CI is green, including `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, lint, max-lines ratchet, compact shards, and `openclaw/ci-gate`
- 311 affected tests passed in WSL across shared state, Doctor, health contributions, lifecycle state, workspace, provenance, MCP, cron, and CLI
- focused Oxlint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and Kysely guardrails pass
- absent/pre-Claws tests prove the collector creates no state and changes no bytes
- existing-state coverage compares database bytes, mtime, mode, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`, and `journal_mode`; WAL regression coverage proves uncheckpointed migrations remain visible
- invalid and newer-schema tests prove open failures become structured findings and handles close cleanly

## Real behavior proof

Exact head `da408dbdf1b92a31baa626c3b64b7819e751258a`, Node 24.15.0 on Ubuntu 24.04 WSL2.

1. Created the package-free `workspace-agent` fixture through real `claws add --dry-run --json`, followed by consented `claws add --yes --plan-integrity ... --json`.
2. Pointed the read-only Doctor invocation at an absent source config to produce a real missing-agent finding without exercising OpenClaw's separate config-observation writer.
3. Held a concurrent SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` writer open with `openclaw.sqlite-wal` and `openclaw.sqlite-shm` present.
4. Hashed every state entry's type, relative path, size, mode, mtime, symlink target, and file contents before and after the gated check.

```text
OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS unset:
{"ok":false,"checksRun":0,"checksSkipped":52,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/lint-selection","severity":"error","message":"Unknown health check id selected by --only: core/doctor/claws-state.","path":"core/doctor/claws-state"}]}

OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1:
STATE_SIDECARS=present
CONCURRENT_WRITER=held-immediate-transaction
BEFORE=4ab862fdbd27b84ecf0c329a4c45eb51d3dd238e54bea3df0532ce6a2837854c
AFTER=4ab862fdbd27b84ecf0c329a4c45eb51d3dd238e54bea3df0532ce6a2837854c
UNCHANGED=yes
{"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":52,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/claws-state","severity":"warning","message":"Claw-owned agent \"workspace-agent\" is missing from config.","source":"doctor","path":"agents.list.workspace-agent","target":"workspace-agent","requirement":"Claw-owned agent config should match its recorded install digest","fixHint":"Inspect the agent change before removing or replacing Claw-owned state."}]}
```

The exit code is `1` because the intentionally induced warning is reported. Private paths are redacted.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102406 MCP ownership
- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics
- Next: #102959 uses the same ownership model for grouped update planning

Doctor lands after every add/remove owner so it can reuse one authoritative status model instead of inventing partial resource checks. The Claws CLI and doctor surface remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

target.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a browser navigation or action invalidates the selected raw target, `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate` retried once and then adopted **any** sole remaining tab, regardless of whether that tab matched the acted-on page:

```ts
if (options?.allowSingleTabFallback && tabs.length === 1) {
  return { targetId: tabs[0]?.targetId ?? opts.oldTargetId, shouldRetry: false };
}
```

The shared resolver backs both `/navigate` and `/act`. So if an action closed or replaced the selected target while an unrelated tab stayed open at a different URL, `/act` could return that unrelated tab's `targetId`. A caller that trusts the response then continues its next mutating action on the wrong page. The focused test even asserted this: old target `old-123`, sole unrelated tab `only-tab` at a different URL, expected result `only-tab`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sole-tab adoption, tab ordering, and a bare URL match are not proof of identity. The response target must be the backend-owned identity of the page that actually executed the operation. When that identity is gone and continuity cannot be proven, the resolver should return the acted-on (now stale or closed) identity so the caller requires a fresh selection, rather than guessing a tab.

The codebase already draws this distinction elsewhere: the post-interaction navigation guard separates newly-appeared tabs from pre-existing ones by their initial target ids, and default tab selection returns `null` ("require a fresh explicit choice") when a sticky target disappears without a proven migration. This change brings the post-action resolver up to the same standard.

## User Impact

A replacement is now adopted only when continuity is provable:

- **Provable replacement (with a pre-action snapshot):** the acted-on page was replaced by a target that did **not** exist before the operation. Exactly one such newly-appeared target is adopted. A pre-existing unrelated tab is never adopted, which fixes the reported wrong-tab routing.
- **Provable renderer swap (navigate path):** exactly one candidate now sits at the URL we just navigated to (Chrome detaches the old renderer target and reattaches the same tab under a new raw target). URL equality is trusted only against the just-navigated URL, never a stale pre-action URL, tab ordering, or a sole remaining tab.
- **Unproven:** the backend-owned acted-on identity is returned so the caller re-selects.

The `/act` route now snapshots tab ids just before the Playwright action and passes them to the resolver. Prior continuity is preserved: `chrome-extension://` to HTTPS navigation (#25323 / #25326) and action-triggered target replacement (#46137) still resolve to the correct replacement.

## Evidence

### Live browser proof (real Chrome over CDP)

A standalone harness (`extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts`) launches a real Chrome instance and reads its live targets through `Target.getTargets`, the same CDP surface the plugin's `listTabs` uses. The genuine raw target ids and URLs are fed into the shipped `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate`. Nothing is mocked; URLs are redacted in the transcript.

Run:

```
pnpm exec tsx extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts
```

Redacted output:

```
=== Live-browser proof for #103785 (real Chrome over CDP) ===

Scenario A: action closes acted-on tab A; unrelated tab B survives

  pre-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>
    - target=19F1C22F… url=data:<ACTED-ON-A>
  post-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>

  resolver returned target=19F1C22F… (A=19F1C22F…, B=48DEEFC6…)
  kept acted-on identity A: true
  adopted unrelated survivor B: false
  PASS: unrelated survivor B was NOT adopted.

Scenario B: renderer swap (old raw target detached, page reattaches at navigated url)

  pre-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=7AC30457… url=data:<PRE-SWAP>
  post-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=F4202B71… url=data:<SWAPPED>

  resolver returned target=F4202B71… (old=7AC30457…, reattached=F4202B71…)
  adopted reattached target at navigated url: true
  PASS: renderer-swap continuity preserved.

=== ALL SCENARIOS PASSED ===
```

- **Scenario A (the reported bug):** tab A is acted on and closed while an unrelated tab B stays open. After the action only B remains, yet the resolver returns A's backend-owned identity and never adopts B. Before this change the sole-tab fallback would have returned B and routed the next action onto the wrong page.
- **Scenario B (continuity preserved):** the acted-on raw target is detached and the page reattaches under a new raw target at the just-navigated URL. The resolver adopts the reattached target, so renderer-swap / action-triggered replacement paths keep working.

### Source and test changes

- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot-target.ts`: removed the sole-tab fallback; adopt only a uniquely newly-appeared target, or the single candidate at the just-navigated URL.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts`: capture pre-action target ids (reusing the existing-session `initialTabTargetIds`, and a new snapshot for the Playwright path) and pass them as `knownTargetIds`.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts`: the "sole unrelated tab" case now asserts the acted-on identity is kept; added a regression test for a sole tab matching only a stale URL.

Automated tests (focused + full browser extension suite):

```
pnpm test:extension browser -- extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts
# Test Files 2 passed (2) | Tests 34 passed (34)

pnpm test:extension browser
# Tests 1887 passed | 1 skipped
# (the only failure, doctor-browser "skips Chrome auto-detection", also fails on a clean checkout: it depends on a local Chrome install)
```

Extension package boundary typecheck: `extension package boundary check passed`.

Closes #103785

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.36.2 to 4.37.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.37.1

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

v4.37.0

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

v4.36.3

No user facing changes.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.37.1 - 16 Jul 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

4.37.0 - 08 Jul 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

target.title: fix(heartbeat): remove dead single-line HTML comment checks in isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` in the heartbeat module contained three unreachable `/^<!--.*-->$/` checks, adding unnecessary maintenance burden. The `stripHeartbeatHtmlComments` preprocessing step called at the top of the function strips leading HTML-comment scaffolding from each line before the loop body runs, so none of the inline checks can ever match.

The inline checks were introduced across two separate PRs (#86627 and #90431) whose authors both saw existing inline HTML-comment checks in the loop and naturally added more on top, not realizing those checks were themselves unreachable. The root cause is a structural overlap in responsibilities: the preprocessing layer and the loop body both claim ownership of HTML comment handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rather than leave dead code with a comment warning future readers not to touch it, this PR removes all three unreachable checks and adds a single comment at the preprocessing call site explaining the division of labor — `stripHeartbeatHtmlComments` (leading-only) owns HTML-comment stripping, and the loop body does not repeat them.

This aligns `isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` with the pattern already used by `parseHeartbeatTasks`, which calls the same preprocessing function and has never had inline HTML-comment checks in its loop — confirming the pattern works correctly.

## User Impact

No user-visible impact. This is a dead-code removal with zero behavioral change.

## Evidence

- **Formal proof**: The `stripLeadingHtmlCommentScaffolding` while-loop condition (`state.inHtmlComment || remaining.trimStart().startsWith("<!--")`) guarantees that on loop exit, the output does not start with `<!--`. Therefore `/^<!--.*-->$/` can never match on the trimmed result after preprocessing.
- **Brute-force validation**: 10,000 randomly generated strings containing `<!--` at random positions were tested — zero produced a line matching `/^<!--.*-->$/` after preprocessing.
- **All existing test cases pass**: 32 tests in `heartbeat.test.ts` + 5 tests in `workspace-templates.test.ts` — all green with no modification.
- **Real behavior proof** — live validation using the actual production source (`npx tsx` loading `src/auto-reply/heartbeat.js` directly):

```
=== Modified isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty behavior ===

  [PASS] single-line HTML comment (bundled template)
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] multi-line HTML comment
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] commented-out tasks block
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] two HTML comments on one line
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] comment then header
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] text before inline comment (not scaffolding)
         expected: false, got: false
  [PASS] plain HTML comment
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] HTML comment then header
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] header only
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] actionable list item
         expected: false, got: false
  [PASS] empty string
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] whitespace only
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] fence opener
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] fenced content with task
         expected: false, got: false
  [PASS] empty list item stub
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] headers only
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] mixed content with prose
         expected: false, got: false

=== After stripHeartbeatHtmlComments: can /^<!--.*-->$/ match? ===

  No matches — all three removed inline checks were dead code.
```

- **Net diff**: 6 insertions, 11 deletions, one file changed.

---

target.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a browser navigation or action invalidates the selected raw target, `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate` retried once and then adopted **any** sole remaining tab, regardless of whether that tab matched the acted-on page:

```ts
if (options?.allowSingleTabFallback && tabs.length === 1) {
  return { targetId: tabs[0]?.targetId ?? opts.oldTargetId, shouldRetry: false };
}
```

The shared resolver backs both `/navigate` and `/act`. So if an action closed or replaced the selected target while an unrelated tab stayed open at a different URL, `/act` could return that unrelated tab's `targetId`. A caller that trusts the response then continues its next mutating action on the wrong page. The focused test even asserted this: old target `old-123`, sole unrelated tab `only-tab` at a different URL, expected result `only-tab`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sole-tab adoption, tab ordering, and a bare URL match are not proof of identity. The response target must be the backend-owned identity of the page that actually executed the operation. When that identity is gone and continuity cannot be proven, the resolver should return the acted-on (now stale or closed) identity so the caller requires a fresh selection, rather than guessing a tab.

The codebase already draws this distinction elsewhere: the post-interaction navigation guard separates newly-appeared tabs from pre-existing ones by their initial target ids, and default tab selection returns `null` ("require a fresh explicit choice") when a sticky target disappears without a proven migration. This change brings the post-action resolver up to the same standard.

## User Impact

A replacement is now adopted only when continuity is provable:

- **Provable replacement (with a pre-action snapshot):** the acted-on page was replaced by a target that did **not** exist before the operation. Exactly one such newly-appeared target is adopted. A pre-existing unrelated tab is never adopted, which fixes the reported wrong-tab routing.
- **Provable renderer swap (navigate path):** exactly one candidate now sits at the URL we just navigated to (Chrome detaches the old renderer target and reattaches the same tab under a new raw target). URL equality is trusted only against the just-navigated URL, never a stale pre-action URL, tab ordering, or a sole remaining tab.
- **Unproven:** the backend-owned acted-on identity is returned so the caller re-selects.

The `/act` route now snapshots tab ids just before the Playwright action and passes them to the resolver. Prior continuity is preserved: `chrome-extension://` to HTTPS navigation (#25323 / #25326) and action-triggered target replacement (#46137) still resolve to the correct replacement.

## Evidence

### Live browser proof (real Chrome over CDP)

A standalone harness (`extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts`) launches a real Chrome instance and reads its live targets through `Target.getTargets`, the same CDP surface the plugin's `listTabs` uses. The genuine raw target ids and URLs are fed into the shipped `resolveTargetIdAfterNavigate`. Nothing is mocked; URLs are redacted in the transcript.

Run:

```
pnpm exec tsx extensions/browser/scripts/proof-103785-target-continuity.mts
```

Redacted output:

```
=== Live-browser proof for #103785 (real Chrome over CDP) ===

Scenario A: action closes acted-on tab A; unrelated tab B survives

  pre-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>
    - target=19F1C22F… url=data:<ACTED-ON-A>
  post-action targets (real CDP):
    - target=48DEEFC6… url=data:<UNRELATED-B>

  resolver returned target=19F1C22F… (A=19F1C22F…, B=48DEEFC6…)
  kept acted-on identity A: true
  adopted unrelated survivor B: false
  PASS: unrelated survivor B was NOT adopted.

Scenario B: renderer swap (old raw target detached, page reattaches at navigated url)

  pre-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=7AC30457… url=data:<PRE-SWAP>
  post-navigate targets (real CDP):
    - target=F4202B71… url=data:<SWAPPED>

  resolver returned target=F4202B71… (old=7AC30457…, reattached=F4202B71…)
  adopted reattached target at navigated url: true
  PASS: renderer-swap continuity preserved.

=== ALL SCENARIOS PASSED ===
```

- **Scenario A (the reported bug):** tab A is acted on and closed while an unrelated tab B stays open. After the action only B remains, yet the resolver returns A's backend-owned identity and never adopts B. Before this change the sole-tab fallback would have returned B and routed the next action onto the wrong page.
- **Scenario B (continuity preserved):** the acted-on raw target is detached and the page reattaches under a new raw target at the just-navigated URL. The resolver adopts the reattached target, so renderer-swap / action-triggered replacement paths keep working.

### Source and test changes

- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot-target.ts`: removed the sole-tab fallback; adopt only a uniquely newly-appeared target, or the single candidate at the just-navigated URL.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts`: capture pre-action target ids (reusing the existing-session `initialTabTargetIds`, and a new snapshot for the Playwright path) and pass them as `knownTargetIds`.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts`: the "sole unrelated tab" case now asserts the acted-on identity is kept; added a regression test for a sole tab matching only a stale URL.

Automated tests (focused + full browser extension suite):

```
pnpm test:extension browser -- extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts
# Test Files 2 passed (2) | Tests 34 passed (34)

pnpm test:extension browser
# Tests 1887 passed | 1 skipped
# (the only failure, doctor-browser "skips Chrome auto-detection", also fails on a clean checkout: it depends on a local Chrome install)
```

Extension package boundary typecheck: `extension package boundary check passed`.

Closes #103785

target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Boot-echo guard chunking used `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units and can split surrogate pairs (emoji, CJK beyond BMP, etc.), producing malformed chunks. This caused the substantial-echo comparison to miss matches when the alignment boundary falls inside a surrogate pair. Replace `.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` to preserve surrogate pair integrity during chunk extraction.

What changed: `getBootPromptChunks` and `containsSubstantialBootEcho` now use `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen()` (wraps `sliceUtf16Safe` from normalization-core) instead of `String.prototype.slice()`, with extended range to compensate for surrogate boundary trimming. What did NOT change: algorithm, chunking logic, cache structure, public API, or behavior for ASCII/BMP-only text.

Fixes #110641

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The boot-echo guard fails to detect echoes when the boot prompt or outbound text contains characters outside the BMP (surrogate pairs), because `String.prototype.slice()` can split a surrogate pair and produce an invalid UTF-16 string that won't match the corresponding chunk.

**Root Cause**: In `src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.ts`, both `getBootPromptChunks()` (line 59) and `containsSubstantialBootEcho()` (line 113) used `haystack.slice(i, i + minLen)` to extract comparison substrings. `String.prototype.slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when `i` falls on a low surrogate, the resulting string is malformed.

**Solution**: Replace `String.prototype.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. A helper `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen()` extends the range by up to 6 code units to compensate for surrogate pair trimming at slice boundaries, ensuring the returned chunk always has at least `minLen` characters.

## Evidence

Current HEAD: ecf8f1045f941a39a288e9599e6827cee5299779

**Behavior addressed**: Boot-echo guard chunking using `String.prototype.slice()` could split UTF-16 surrogate pairs, causing echo detection misses for boot prompts containing emoji or extended CJK characters.

**Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic, Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw worktree at `ecf8f1045f9`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# 1. Demonstrate sliceUtf16Safe preserves surrogate pairs where String.slice breaks
node --import tsx -e "
import { sliceUtf16Safe } from '@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice';
const text = 'Hello\u{1F600}World';
console.log('String.slice(5,6) length:', text.slice(5,6).length, '(broken surrogate)');
console.log('sliceUtf16Safe(5,7) length:', sliceUtf16Safe(text,5,7).length, '(preserved)');
"
# 2. Integration test with actual boot-echo-guard module
node --import tsx -e "
import { stripBootEchoFromOutboundText } from './src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.js';
const emoji = '\u{1F600}';
const boot = ['BOOT.md:','Wake up ' + emoji + ' and send greeting','over configured channel'].join('\n');
const echo = 'Wake up ' + emoji + ' and send greeting over configured channel';
console.log('Echo detected:', stripBootEchoFromOutboundText(echo, boot) === '' ? 'YES' : 'NO');
"
# 3. Full test suite
npx vitest run src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { sliceUtf16Safe } from '@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice'; const text = 'Hello\u{1F600}World'; console.log('String.slice(5,6) length:', text.slice(5,6).length, '(broken)'); console.log('sliceUtf16Safe(5,7) length:', sliceUtf16Safe(text,5,7).length, '(preserved)');"
stdout:
String.slice(5,6) length: 1 (broken)
sliceUtf16Safe(5,7) length: 2 (preserved)

$ node --import tsx -e "import { stripBootEchoFromOutboundText } from './src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.js'; const emoji = '\u{1F600}'; const boot = ['BOOT.md:','Wake up ' + emoji + ' and send greeting','over configured channel'].join('\n'); const echo = 'Wake up ' + emoji + ' and send greeting over configured channel'; console.log('Echo detected:', stripBootEchoFromOutboundText(echo, boot) === '' ? 'YES' : 'NO');"
```

## Summary

`loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` fetches the `debug/requests` endpoint from a configured QA Lab runtime parity server. When the endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status (503, 400, 500), the function returns null early without consuming the response body stream, leaving an unread stream resource dangling that may hold the connection open.

The fix adds `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the early return on `!response.ok`. This cancels the unread body stream, matching the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path.

**What changed**: One line added in `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` at `runtime-parity.ts:1055`. No changes to the ok path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the ok response path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality. No new dependencies or configuration options added.

Fixes #109991

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` returns null early on non-ok HTTP responses without cancelling the unread response body stream, potentially leaking resources and holding connections open.

**Root Cause**: At `runtime-parity.ts:1055`, the `!response.ok` early-return path calls `return null` without first cancelling the response body stream via `response.body?.cancel()`. The ok path implicitly drains the body via `response.json()`, but the non-ok path has no such cleanup.

**Solution**: Add `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before returning null on non-ok responses. This mirrors the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path. The `.catch(() => undefined)` guard ensures safety even if the body stream is already in an inconsistent state.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body in crabline injection
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109992

**What changed**: Added `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the `postCrablineInbound()` error path. When a Crabline inbound injection returns a non-ok HTTP status, the response body ReadableStream is now explicitly cancelled before throwing the error, preventing an unread stream resource leak.

**What NOT changed**: No change to the happy path — successful responses still pass through to the complete handler as before. No change to the Crabline injection logic, request construction, or error message format. No new dependencies added.

**merge-risk**: Minimal — the pattern `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` is a standard no-op on success and a no-throw guard on failure. It affects only the single error path in `crabline-transport.ts`. Zero risk of regression on the ok path.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a Crabline inbound injection HTTP request returns a non-ok response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is left unread, causing a potential resource leak (unconsumed ReadableStream). Node.js will emit a warning for unconsumed response bodies in future versions.

**Root Cause**: `postCrablineInbound()` throws immediately in the `if (!response.ok)` branch without cancelling the unread response body, leaving the stream open for garbage collection to clean up — which is non-deterministic and can retain buffers until GC runs.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the error path to eagerly release the stream. The `cancel()` method (Fetch API standard) releases the stream's resources. The `?.` optional chaining guards against a null body (e.g., 204 No Content responses or server errors that omit a body). The `.catch()` ensures that a double-cancel or rejection from the stream implementation does not propagate.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: When a Crabline inbound injection receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is now explicitly cancelled before the error is thrown, eliminating a resource leak from an unconsumed ReadableStream.

target.title: fix(openai-http): keep SSE argument chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Replace `String.prototype.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` in `splitArgumentsForStreaming` to prevent SSE argument chunks from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. The old code could produce invalid JSON when multi-byte characters (e.g., CJK, emoji) straddled the 256-char chunk boundary, causing downstream parse failures on the client.

Fixes #110642

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: SSE streaming chunks of tool_call arguments can contain truncated/invalid UTF-16 when the 256-char boundary falls inside a surrogate pair, causing the client to receive malformed JSON.

**Root Cause**: `splitArgumentsForStreaming()` in `src/gateway/openai-http.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units without awareness of surrogate pairs. When a multi-byte character spans positions 255-256, the slice produces a broken chunk.

**Solution**: Import and use `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, which ensures surrogate pairs are never split. The loop increment is changed from a fixed `+= chunkSize` to `+= chunk.length` (with `|| 1` fallback) because the safe slice may return 256 or 257 characters.

target.title: fix(matrix): journal inbound events before advancing sync token
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix loses inbound user messages when the gateway crashes or restarts while an agent turn is running.

The loss window is structural: matrix-js-sdk's `doSync` sets the sync token **before** processing the batch's events ("set the sync token NOW *before* processing the events … so if something barfs on an event we can skip it" — `node_modules/matrix-js-sdk/lib/sync.js:725-728`). The plugin's `SqliteBackedMatrixSyncStore.setSyncData` then persists that token (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/file-sync-store.ts:227-232`, 250 ms debounce). Meanwhile the SDK bridge re-emits the event synchronously (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk.ts:2073-2086`) and the monitor dispatched it **detached** into a memory-only `KeyedAsyncQueue` (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts:539`) for the full agent-turn duration.

So the sequence was: message arrives → token advanced in memory → next `/sync` tells the homeserver the batch is consumed → token persisted to SQLite — all while the message still sits in a memory-only queue. Any crash in that window (routinely minutes, the whole agent turn) permanently loses the message. The existing persistent inbound deduper only stores dedupe records, not the payload, so nothing can replay it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same crash window the durable-ingress fleet adoption (#109657) already closed on the sibling channels — telegram (#108924), discord (#110274), whatsapp (#110418), mattermost (#110386), msteams (#110357), slack (#109910), signal (#109907), imessage (#110409), sms (#109866) — and Matrix is the remaining sync-loop channel still on detached in-memory dispatch. This PR mirrors the merged Mattermost adapter (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-ingress.ts`) one-for-one, mapped onto Matrix's ack equivalent (the sync-token persist instead of a websocket receive):

- New `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/ingress.ts`: every dispatchable inbound event (room message, decrypted message, reaction) is journaled into the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue **synchronously inside the sync event listener**. The queue's SQLite write is a synchronous transaction (`src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts` `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`), so the journal row commits in the same macrotask cycle — before the 250 ms-debounced token persist can tell the homeserver the batch is consumed. Durable-before-ack.
- Dispatch now runs through the core durable ingress drain (`createChannelIngressDrain`) with per-room lanes (`room:<id>`, matching the handler's existing per-room serialization), the canonical `turnAdoptionLifecycle` seam (`bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` → `core.channel.inbound.run`, so the claim tombstones at adoption when the turn's recovery state is durable), bounded retry with backoff and dead-letter (8 attempts / 24 h, shared defaults), and startup replay of journaled rows.
- Handler failures now propagate to the drain when journaled (the detached path swallowed them) so the retry/dead-letter policy owns them; terminal non-turn outcomes (policy gates, dedupe skips) tombstone on dispatch return. The pre-existing persistent deduper keeps homeserver redeliveries exactly-once on top of the drain's tombstones.
- Events without an `event_id` cannot be journaled and keep the previous live-dispatch path (`onUnjournaledEvent`), matching the handler's existing fail-open dedupe behavior for unidentifiable events.
- Journal-append failure retries (0/100/300 ms) then drops loudly (fail closed), mirroring the whatsapp landing decision; because the journal and the sync-token store share the same state DB, a broken DB fails the token persist too, so the homeserver redelivers after restart.
- Shutdown stops ingress after `drainPendingDecryptions` (those emissions still need the journal) and awaits in-flight drain dispatches exactly where the old detached-task `waitForIdle` stood.

No SQLite schema change (reuses the existing `channel_ingress_events` table in the shared state DB), no new config or env surface, no core/SDK changes — the adapter only consumes the already-exported seams (`createChannelIngressDrain`, `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions`, `state.openChannelIngressQueue`).

Known boundary (follow-up candidate, out of scope): E2EE events are journaled when the decrypt bridge emits the decrypted event; a crash between token persist and decryption still loses the still-encrypted event. Closing that needs re-injecting raw encrypted events into the crypto pipeline on replay, which is a separate design.

## User Impact

- A gateway crash/restart during (or before) an agent turn no longer permanently loses Matrix room messages, decrypted messages, or reactions: journaled events replay once on startup and are deduped against already-handled ones.
- Handler failures retry with bounded backoff and dead-letter loudly instead of vanishing into a detached-task log line.
- No operator action, config change, or migration required; behavior on the happy path is unchanged (same per-room serialization, same reply pipeline).

## Evidence

### Loss-window walkthrough (before)

| Step | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `/sync` batch arrives | `node_modules/matrix-js-sdk/lib/sync.js:725-728` | token set **before** event processing |
| token persisted | `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/file-sync-store.ts:227-232` | homeserver may consider batch consumed after 250 ms debounce |
| event re-emitted | `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk.ts:2073-2086` | sync, during batch processing |
| dispatch | `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/events.ts` (old) | detached `void runMonitorTask(...)` into memory-only queue |
| agent turn | `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts:539` | message lives only in process memory for minutes |

Crash anywhere after the persist → message gone. After this PR, the journal row exists in SQLite before the listener returns, the drain dispatches with heartbeats + lane serialization, and rows tombstone only at adoption/completion.

### Regression tests (real SQLite queue, temp state dir, no mocks of the journal path)

New `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/ingress.test.ts` (6 tests) drives the real `channel_ingress_events` queue via `createChannelIngressQueueForTests` over a real temp state DB:

- journal row commits in the same macrotask cycle as `accept()` (before any timer-based persist could fire), dispatch not started;
- **restart replay**: accept → simulated crash (no stop) → fresh monitor over the same state dir dispatches the journaled event exactly once and tombstones it;
- completed events are not redispatched across a restart;
- a throwing dispatch is **not** tombstoned — a later process redelivers it (retry budget), then completes;
- events without an `event_id` fall back to live dispatch and journal nothing;
- end-to-end through the real `registerMatrixMonitorEvents` wiring: a synchronous `room.message` emission (as the SDK bridge does inside `doSync`) is durable immediately after the listener returns, then replays once after a restart.

Plus `handler.test.ts`: the handler threads the ingress lifecycle into `core.channel.inbound.run` as `turnAdoptionLifecycle` (`admission: "exclusive"`, `onAdopted`/`onAbandoned` passthrough). `index.test.ts`: handler failures surface to the drain, and shutdown ordering is pause-sync → drain decryptions → ingress stop (awaits in-flight) → thread-binding stop → client release.

### Test runs

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/ingress.test.ts \
    extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/index.test.ts \
    extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/events.test.ts \
    extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests  211 passed (211)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/
Test Files  35 passed (35)
Tests  484 passed (484)
```

(The full monitor-directory run is intermittently 7-red in `reaction-events.test.ts` with `runtime.state.resolveStateDir is not a function`; reproduced on unmodified `origin/main` 1/4 runs with the identical signature — pre-existing cross-file flake, unrelated to this change.)

### Reverse verification (control-red)

Stashed only the four production files (`events.ts`, `handler.ts`, `index.ts`, `ingress.ts`), kept the tests:

```
Test Files  4 failed (4)   ← ingress import gone, wiring assertions red
Tests  6 failed | 199 passed (205)
```

Restored the fix → same four files green (211/211).

### tsgo / lint / format

```
$ tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json
→ only the 3 pre-existing packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts errors (stale ipaddr.js types); zero in touched files
$ oxlint extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/   → clean
$ oxfmt --check extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/ → clean
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Tool-loop veto records were hashless, so repeated no-progress calls could stop advancing the streak before the global circuit breaker threshold.

## Why This Change Was Made
Loop vetoes now use a stable sentinel hash and the no-progress streak logic counts that sentinel as another no-progress step, so the breaker can keep advancing without treating the veto as progress.

## User Impact
Repeated identical no-progress tool calls can now cross the global circuit breaker as intended after a loop veto.

## Evidence
- Current head: `55904ccab99946c9e58b489d67d7ae79721dd058`
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module -`: replayed two identical no-progress sends, then a `tool-loop` veto; the next `detectToolCallLoop(...)` returned `stuck: true`, `level: critical`, `detector: global_circuit_breaker`, `count: 3`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts`: passed 1 Vitest shard, 57 tests.
- `git diff --check`

Closes #109435

target.title: fix(gateway): trim device.pair approve/reject requestId
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`device.pair.approve` / `device.pair.reject` used `requestId` as pasted, while
the same module already trims `deviceId` and `gateway.suspend.prepare` trims
`requestId`. Clipboard padding produced false `unknown requestId` for a live
pending pair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trim `requestId` once at the start of both handlers before pending-lookup /
approve / reject / broadcast, matching the suspend prepare contract.

## User Impact

**Before:** Approving/rejecting with `" req-… "` failed as unknown.

**After:** Surrounding whitespace is ignored; the pending pairing key still
matches.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/server-methods/devices.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/devices.test.ts`
- Production path: `deviceHandlers["device.pair.approve"|"device.pair.reject"]`
  → `requestId.trim()` → `approveDevicePairing` / `rejectDevicePairing`
- Compatibility: stored pending keys remain unpadded; only the RPC input is
  normalized

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Live Gateway: plant a pending device pairing in an isolated state DB, then
`device.pair.reject` with a padded `requestId` rejects that pending request.
A padded unknown id still returns `unknown requestId`.

### Canonical reachability path

Gateway RPC `device.pair.reject` → trim `requestId` →
`rejectDevicePairing(trimmed)` → respond success with trimmed id

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Same `.trim()` pattern as `gateway.suspend.prepare` (`suspend.ts`) and local
`deviceId.trim()` checks; no new config.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` /
config / `HOME`; loopback Gateway; pending request planted via
`requestDevicePairing` into the same state dir before Gateway start.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# plant pending into OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, then:
node scripts/run-node.mjs devices list --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway call device.pair.reject \
  --params '{"requestId":" <pending-request-id> "}' \
  --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
```

### Evidence after fix

Pending list (redacted):

```json
{
  "pending": [
    {
      "requestId": "c89c6c7c-3264-4e6b-8466-91ed2893087d",
      "deviceId": "proof-device-1",
      "role": "node"
    }
  ],
  "paired": []
}
```

Padded reject succeeds (trimmed id echoed):

```json
{
  "requestId": "c89c6c7c-3264-4e6b-8466-91ed2893087d",
  "deviceId": "proof-device-1"
}
```

Unknown padded id:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "unknown requestId"
  }
}
```

Gateway log also showed a padded approve attempt resolving the same pending
request before role-policy denial (`role-management-requires-admin`), which
confirms lookup-after-trim on the approve path as well.

### Observed result after fix

A padded pending pairing `requestId` resolves through a real Gateway WebSocket
`device.pair.reject` call.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

target.title: fix(gateway): trim cron job ids before exact lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveCronJobId` returned `params.id ?? params.jobId` without trimming, while
nearby cron wake paths already trim `sessionKey` / `agentId`. Padded job ids
made `cron.get` / `cron.run` / `cron.remove` / `cron.update` / `cron.runs`
report not found for existing jobs. `cron.update` also bypassed the helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trim inside `resolveCronJobId` and route `cron.update` through that helper so
every exact job-id lookup shares one normalization point.

## User Impact

**Before:** `" ${jobId} "` failed as missing/not found.

**After:** Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped before store lookup.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts`
- Production path: `cronHandlers` get/run/remove/update/runs →
  `resolveCronJobId` → `context.cron.readJob` / `enqueueRun`
- Compatibility: whitespace-only ids still count as missing

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Live Gateway RPC: create a cron job, then `cron.get` with a padded id returns
the job. Whitespace-only id still returns `INVALID_REQUEST` / missing id.

### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw gateway call cron.get` → `resolveCronJobId` (trim) →
`context.cron.readJob(<trimmed>)` → job payload

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local helper only; aligns with existing cron wake `.trim()` usage; no new
config.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` /
config / `HOME`; loopback Gateway via `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run`;
Node 22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# isolated gateway + token on a free loopback port
node scripts/run-node.mjs cron add --name trim-proof --every 1h --session main \
  --system-event "trim proof heartbeat" --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway call cron.get \
  --params '{"id":" <job-id> "}' --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway call cron.get \
  --params '{"id":"   "}' --url ws://127.0.0.1:$PORT --token $TOKEN --json
```

### Evidence after fix

Redacted live RPC (padded id succeeds):

```json
{
  "id": "24df4718-c0b2-477a-ac33-2d8e1c348684",
  "name": "trim-proof",
  "enabled": true,
  "schedule": { "kind": "every", "everyMs": 3600000 },
  "sessionTarget": "main",
  "payload": { "kind": "systemEvent", "text": "trim proof heartbeat" }
}
```

Whitespace-only id:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "invalid cron.get params: missing id"
  }
}
```

### Observed result after fix

A padded existing cron job id resolves through a real Gateway WebSocket
`cron.get` call; whitespace-only input remains invalid.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): notify users when Codex session changes
target.body:
Related: #106957, #108769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel users could receive no reply when another gateway or session transition superseded the Codex session generation before their message ran. The agent runner logged `Embedded agent failed before reply`, but the generation error was treated as generic; normal group failure policy then converted the reply to `NO_REPLY`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify the stable Codex generation-fence error as a known terminal failure and return a short, redacted retry prompt. This is intentionally not a durable-ingress retry: the channel claim is completed when the turn is adopted, before Codex starts, and replaying an adopted turn can duplicate side effects. The same in-flight turn also keeps the stale physical session ID, so retrying that run cannot reclaim the authoritative generation.

Codex app-server identifies resume/start operations by thread ID and rejoins running threads only inside its current process; it exposes no cross-process generation token. OpenClaw therefore continues to own and enforce this fence. See [`ThreadResumeParams`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b8b61bc692517adcd18622df260f2ddd80635122/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L310-L324), [`TurnStartParams`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b8b61bc692517adcd18622df260f2ddd80635122/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L71-L75), and the process-local running-thread lookup in [`thread_processor.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b8b61bc692517adcd18622df260f2ddd80635122/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L3296-L3344).

## User Impact

Instead of silence, users now receive: `⚠️ This Codex session changed before your message could run. Please send it again.` The physical session identifier is never exposed. The underlying generation fence and no-replay behavior are unchanged.

Release-note context: fixes silent channel drops when a Codex session generation changes before an adopted turn starts.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxv416r7z3df45ydepkhzvy7`: focused terminal-failure suite passed 20/20; full changed gate passed (format, boundaries, production/test typechecks, lint, and guards). [Run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29653800465)
- Regression covers a Telegram group turn, asserts a non-silent final reply, exact actionable copy, and session-ID redaction.
- Fresh uncommitted autoreview: clean, correctness confidence 0.97.
- Live two-gateway/channel proof was not run: no deterministic source-blind fixture exists without an approved private channel or internal state injection.

AI-assisted: implementation and review performed with Codex.

target.title: fix(doctor): bound session snapshot store reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor session-snapshot scan/repair loaded session store JSON with unbounded
`fs.readFileSync` at two call sites. A corrupted or hostile multi-GB
`sessions.json` under the user state directory could OOM `openclaw doctor`
before JSON parse or repair logic ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a shared `readSnapshotStoreRaw` helper with `statSync` +
`MAX_SNAPSHOT_STORE_BYTES = 16 MiB`, and route both the scan loader and the
repair backup read through it. Oversized stores fail closed: doctor emits an
operator-visible Session snapshots note, structured health issues use
`kind: "store-too-large"`, and repair effects record
`would-skip-oversized-session-store`.

## User Impact

**Before:** An oversized session store could force an unbounded sync string
alloc during doctor snapshot health, or be skipped silently with no operator
signal.

**After:** Stores above 16 MiB are rejected before `readFileSync`. Doctor
reports the skip, and normal stores continue to scan/repair.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.ts`,
  `src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts`
- Production path: `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` /
  `noteSessionSnapshotHealth` → `loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` /
  repair `updateSessionStore` callback → `readSnapshotStoreRaw`
- Compatibility: normal stores unchanged; oversized stores are skipped with a
  warning instead of crashing the process

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

A ~17 MiB session store is not passed to `readFileSync`. Isolated
`openclaw doctor --non-interactive --yes` prints a Session snapshots note that
the store was skipped as oversized.

### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw doctor` → session snapshot health →
`noteSessionSnapshotHealth` / `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` →
`loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` → `readSnapshotStoreRaw` (stat + 16 MiB cap)
→ skip + warn on overflow

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Same bound pattern as other doctor store caps; no new config/env keys.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; Node 22.23.1; isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `HOME` under `/tmp` with a
planted 17 MiB `sessions.json`; CLI via
`node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes` after local build.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
PROOF=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-doctor-snap-proof-XXXXXX)
STATE=$PROOF/state; HOME_DIR=$PROOF/home; CONFIG=$PROOF/openclaw.json
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR" "$STATE/agents/main/sessions"
printf '%s\n' '{"agents":{"list":[{"id":"main","default":true}]}}' > "$CONFIG"
# write 17 MiB of bytes to $STATE/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$CONFIG CI=true \
  node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes
```

Focused regression:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts \
  -t "oversized session stores" --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

Redacted CLI:

```text
◇  Session snapshots ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - Skipped oversized session store                                                    │
│    .../state/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json                                       │
│    (.../sessions.json: file too large (17825792 bytes, max 16777216)).                │
│    Snapshot-path health was not scanned.                                              │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Focused tests:

```text
✓ reports oversized session stores without reading them into memory
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 24 skipped (25)
```

### Observed result after fix

Real `openclaw doctor` warns and skips the oversized store; `readFileSync` is
never called for that path during snapshot scan.

target.title: fix(doctor): stream JSONL line counts without full-file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` state integrity counted main-session JSONL transcript lines by
`fs.readFileSync` + walking every character. A multi-hundred-MB transcript forced
the whole file into one UTF-8 string before the `lineCount <= 1` warning could
run, so doctor could spike RSS to roughly the transcript size.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the full-file string read with a fixed-size sync chunk reader
(`openSync` + `readSync`) that counts `0x0a` bytes and preserves the old
trailing-newline rule for the final incomplete line. Close failures stay inside
the helper so an uncommon `closeSync` error cannot abort doctor after a
successful count.

## User Impact

**Before:** A large main transcript could make `openclaw doctor` allocate a
full-file string just to count lines. A close failure after chunked counting
could also abort the doctor command.

**After:** Line counting streams 64 KiB chunks, so doctor keeps the
single-line warning without buffering the whole transcript, and close errors
remain fail-soft.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts`,
  `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts`
- Production path: `noteStateIntegrity` → main transcript exists →
  `countJsonlLines(transcriptPath)` → `lineCount <= 1` warning
- Compatibility: empty / missing / single-line / multi-line semantics unchanged;
  only the read strategy and close fail-soft boundary change

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Isolated `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --yes` against a one-line main
transcript prints the State integrity warning; the same command against an
8 × 64 KiB multi-chunk transcript does not.

### Canonical reachability path

`openclaw doctor` → `noteStateIntegrity` → resolve main session transcript →
`countJsonlLines` (chunked `readSync`) → optional
`Main session transcript has only … line` warning

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local to doctor state integrity; no new config/env surface. Chunk size matches
the existing doctor JSONL reader constant family (64 KiB).

### Real environment tested

Local trusted source checkout at PR head; Node 22.23.1; isolated
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `HOME` under `/tmp`; CLI via
`node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes` after local build.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# one-line
PROOF=$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-doctor-jsonl-proof-XXXXXX)
STATE=$PROOF/state; HOME_DIR=$PROOF/home; CONFIG=$PROOF/openclaw.json
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR" "$STATE/agents/main/sessions"
printf '%s\n' '{"agents":{"list":[{"id":"main","default":true}]}}' > "$CONFIG"
printf '%s' '{"type":"session"}' > "$STATE/agents/main/sessions/short-main.jsonl"
printf '%s\n' '{"agent:main:main":{"sessionId":"short-main","updatedAt":1700000000000}}' \
  > "$STATE/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json"
HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_HOME=$HOME_DIR OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$CONFIG CI=true \
  node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive --yes

# multi-chunk (8 × 64 KiB lines; ~512 KiB)
# rewrite sessions.json to chunked-main.jsonl, then rerun the same doctor command
```

Focused regression (closeSync fail-soft):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts \
  -t "multi-chunk|only one line|closeSync" --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
│  - Main session transcript has only 1 line. Session history may not be   │
│    appending.                                                            │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

target.title: fix(qqbot): log tool media failures after block replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When QQBot had already delivered a block reply and later flushed tool-collected
media URLs, `outbound-dispatch.ts` wrapped `sendMedia` in an empty `catch {}`
and ignored `result.error`. Upload/send failures were silent: the turn looked
successful while tool images/files never reached the user.

The tool-only fallback path already logged via `sendToolMediaWithTimeout`,
which closes over and forwards `...gatewayMediaContext` (workspaceDir /
mediaAccess) into `sendMedia`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `sendToolMediaWithTimeout` for the post-block tool-media flush so thrown
failures and `result.error` are logged with the same timeout/budget behavior
and the same `gatewayMediaContext` forwarding as the tool-only path.

## User Impact

**Before:** Tool media after a visible block reply could fail with no log.

**After:** Failures are logged
(`Tool media send error after block response: …`) while agent-scoped local
media roots still resolve through `gatewayMediaContext`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts`
- Production path: `deliver(block)` → `deliver(tool mediaUrl)` →
  `hasBlockResponse && toolMediaUrls` → `sendToolMediaWithTimeout` →
  `sendMedia({ ...gatewayMediaContext })` → `log.error` on failure

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. Rejected post-block `sendMedia` is logged (no empty catch).
2. Agent-scoped local tool media after a block still resolves to the workspace
   file path (proves `gatewayMediaContext` is still forwarded by the helper).
3. The same local-root path also logs when the send rejects.

### Canonical reachability path

`dispatchOutbound` → buffered block deliver → tool media deliver →
`sendToolMediaWithTimeout` (closes over `gatewayMediaContext`) →
`sendMedia` / `log.error`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses existing `sendToolMediaWithTimeout` (already spreads
`...gatewayMediaContext` on every call). No send-contract narrowing.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted checkout; production `dispatchOutbound` caller with real temp
workspace file + mocked sender reject. Node v22.23.1; PR head `3c7b10c8ea9`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts -t "logs tool media|keeps agent-scoped media roots on post-block|threads agent scoped media roots through gateway tool media" --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
✓ threads agent scoped media roots through gateway tool media forwarding 40ms
✓ logs tool media send failures after a block response instead of swallowing them 16ms
✓ keeps agent-scoped media roots on post-block tool media while logging send errors 21ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed | 42 skipped (45)
```

### Observed result after fix

- `log.error` receives
  `Tool media send error after block response: upload exploded`.
- Post-block local tool media still calls sender with
  `source: { localPath: <realpath under agent workspace> }` (context preserved)
  and still logs on reject.

### What was not tested

Live QQ Bot API upload against a real account. Proof is the production
`dispatchOutbound` path with a real workspace file and mocked transport reject.

### Fix classification

bugfix — silent media delivery failure

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted implementation and proof.

target.title: fix(ui): stream-decode terminal startup UTF-8 chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI terminal startup input used a module-level `TextDecoder` and called
`decode(bytes)` without `{ stream: true }`. Before a Gateway session is bound,
pasted CJK/emoji can arrive as UTF-8 split across WebSocket/libterminal chunks.
Without stream mode, a mid-sequence chunk becomes U+FFFD mojibake in the
pending input buffer.

An earlier revision incorrectly flushed the decoder on session adoption, which
could finalize a partial scalar as U+FFFD when the completing byte arrived
after bind. This revision keeps the decoder open across adoption and only
flushes on tab dispose.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Decode each chunk with `{ stream: true }`
- Keep decoder state across session adoption (drain buffer only)
- Flush only on dispose
- Regression: bind between bytes of one UTF-8 scalar (`E4 B8` then `AD` → `中`)
- Negative control: non-stream decode of the same split produces U+FFFD

## User Impact

**Before:** Pasting CJK/emoji while a terminal tab is still connecting could
corrupt characters that straddled chunk boundaries (and an adopt-time flush
could make that worse).

**After:** Split UTF-8 sequences reassemble across pre-bind and post-bind
chunks; incomplete trailers flush only when the tab is disposed.

## Evidence

- Changed: `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-startup-input.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-startup-input.test.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel.ts`
- Production path: Ghostty `onData` → `createTerminalStartupInput.onData`
  (`decode(..., { stream: true })`) → pending buffer → `adoptSession` drain
  (decoder stays open) → later `onData` completes scalar → Gateway `input`

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. Byte-split UTF-8 for `中😀` reassembles with no U+FFFD before session bind.
2. Session bind between `E4 B8` and `AD` still yields `中` (decoder not flushed).
3. Non-stream `TextDecoder` on the same split produces U+FFFD (negative control).

### Canonical reachability path

`createTerminalStartupInput.onData` → streaming `TextDecoder` →
`BoundedBuffer` / live `connection.input` after `getSessionId()` becomes set →
`adoptSession` drains complete buffer text only → dispose calls `flush()`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses the platform `TextDecoder` stream contract; no new deps.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted checkout exercising the production `createTerminalStartupInput`
helper used by `terminal-panel.ts` (same `onData` / adopt / dispose seams).
Node v22.23.1; PR head `e26c948b840`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-startup-input.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
✓ reassembles UTF-8 code points split across WebSocket chunks before session bind 1ms
✓ does not emit U+FFFD for a mid-sequence chunk without stream mode regression 0ms
✓ keeps decoder state across session bind so a straddling scalar completes 0ms
✓ proves non-stream decode mojibakes the same split that stream mode keeps intact 0ms
✓ flushes incomplete trailer only on explicit dispose flush 0ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Observed result after fix

- One-byte-per-chunk feed of `中😀` drains as exactly `中😀`.
- Bind between `E4 B8` and `AD` delivers `中` to `connection.input`, not `�`.
- Non-stream decode of the same split contains U+FFFD and is not `中`.

### What was not tested

Manual Control UI paste against a live Gateway terminal session / Crabbox
recording. The production helper + panel adopt/dispose seams are covered above.

### Fix classification

bugfix — UTF-8 chunk / mojibake + lifecycle-boundary decoder state

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted implementation and proof.
